# Auto-generated methods (initer.til)
#
# The initer auto-generates namespace methods for structs and enums
# when the user hasn't defined them. All generation is skipped if the
# method already exists in the namespace: section.
#
# Source of truth: src/self/initer.til

* Structs

** clone := func(val: T) returns T
   Deep-copies all instance fields. ref fields are copied as pointers
   (shared). own fields are cloned recursively. FuncPtr fields are
   copied directly (no clone). Skipped for core ext_structs (C side
   provides clone).

** delete := func(own self: T, call_free: Bool = true)
   Frees all instance fields. own fields call Type.delete(field, true).
   Non-own compound fields call Type.delete(field, false) (cleanup
   without freeing the pointer). ref and FuncPtr fields are skipped.
   Calls free(own self) when call_free is true.

** size := func() returns USize
   The size of a value in the program that EXECUTES the call. The
   generated body is a literal computed from the field layout with
   alignment padding, in the layout of the RUNNING COMPILER: own and ref
   fields are pointers (compact when the compiler itself was built
   ~--usize=32~), ~USize~ and ~UPtr~ fields take the compiler's own
   widths. That literal is what the compile-time interpreter gets, so a
   container moving bytes inside the compiler stays correct.

   The built program never gets that literal. til computes the TARGET's
   layout itself and, when emission starts, replaces every direct call of
   a generated ~size()~ with that number; a generated ~X_size~ that is
   still emitted (dyn dispatch, an export) returns the same number. No C
   ~sizeof~ supplies a size, so compilers built with either layout emit
   the same source for a target. HolyC is the exception: its aggregate
   layout differs from C's and its emitter keeps spelling sizes as its own
   ~sizeof~.

   Not generated: the primitives' and ~Bool~'s ~size~ are hand-written
   literals in core (~U8.size()~ is ~return 1~), and ~USize~ / ~UPtr~ are
   aliases of one of them per target. A function type has no ~size~;
   ~F.size()~ is routed to ~Dynamic.size()~, one pointer. ~Dynamic~'s own
   hand-written ~size~ is replaced by a generated one. A hand-written
   ~size~ on a user type wins and is an ordinary function.

** hash := func(self: T, hasher: HashFn) returns U64
   Generated only when every field is shallow (no own / no ref). This
   avoids bytewise hashing pointer addresses for managed content. Types
   with owned or borrowed fields must define a content-aware hash if they
   need one.

** cmp := func(a: T, b: T) returns I64
   Lexicographic by DECLARATION order: the first field whose ~cmp~ is
   non-zero decides, ties fall through to the next field, all ties means
   equal. Generated under the same rule as ~eq~ -- every instance field
   shallow and comparable -- so a struct with an ~own~ or ~ref~ field, a
   funcptr field, or a field whose type has no ~cmp~ of its own is NOT
   ordered, and using it where ordering is required still fails at the
   use site with "no namespace function 'cmp'".

   That exemption is what keeps CONTAINERS out: ~Vec~, ~Set~, ~Map~ and
   friends hold an ~own~ data buffer, so none of them gets a derived
   ~cmp~ -- ordering them by their fields would compare pointer
   addresses. Types that want an order define ~cmp~ themselves (~Str~
   does), and a hand-written one always wins over the derivation.

   Deriving nothing is deliberate over deriving something that panics: a
   panicking ~cmp~ would let ~Set(Vec(I64))~ compile and die at runtime,
   where today it is a compile error. (#335)

** eq := func(self: T, other: T) returns Bool
   Generated when every instance field is shallow and comparable. Compares
   fields in declaration order and returns false at the first mismatch.
   If the struct defines ~cmp~ -- or gets one derived, which now happens
   whenever the fields allow -- the cmp-derived comparison helpers win.
   Structs with own/ref fields are left to explicit methods for now
   (tracked by #270).

** to_str := func(self: T) returns Str
   Generated when every instance field is shallow and printable. Formats
   the value in constructor style, e.g. ~Color(r=0, g=0, b=0, a=0)~.
   Structs with own/ref fields are left to explicit methods for now
   (tracked by #270).

* Enums

** eq := func(self: E, other: E) returns Bool
   Tag comparison. For payload variants, also compares payloads via
   their type's eq method. FuncPtr payloads use tag-only comparison.
   For payload enums, generation is skipped unless every payload type is
   comparable.

** cmp := func(a: E, b: E) returns I64
   Declaration order: walking variants in order, the first that matches
   either side decides, and two matching payload variants defer to the
   payload's own ~cmp~. A pointer-slot payload compares POINTEES, the
   same rule ~eq~ follows, which is what lets ~Option(ref T)~ be ordered.
   Generated only when every payload type is comparable, so an enum
   carrying an unordered payload stays unordered. (#335)

** is := func(self: E, other: E) returns Bool
   Calls the runtime tag comparison helper.

** clone := func(self: E) returns E
   Payload variants: clone the payload via get_Variant + constructor.
   Simple variants: copy via eq check + constructor.

** delete := func(own self: E, call_free: Bool = true)
   Calls payload delete for managed payload variants, then calls
   free(own self) if call_free.

** size := func() returns USize
   Same contract as the struct ~size~ above. The literal is the enum's
   layout in the running compiler: the tag (~enum(Type)~ picks its width,
   U8 by default), then for payload enums the payload at a fixed offset of
   8 in a slot at least one pointer wide; a niche enum is one pointer.

** to_str := func(self: E) returns Str
   Returns variant name as string. Payload variants append the
   payload's to_str in parens: "Variant(payload)". FuncPtr payloads
   use "Variant(func)". For payload enums, generation is skipped unless
   every payload type is printable.

** Variant constructors / constants
   Tag-only enums get variant constants in the enum namespace. Payload
   enums get one constructor per variant, with payload constructors taking
   the payload value.

* size and size_for_target

  Decided in #472. ~size()~ behaves as described here today.
  ~size_for_target()~ is NOT IMPLEMENTED YET; until it is, a generator
  condition's ~T.size()~ is still answered for the target by a special
  mode (~doc/concepts/functions.org~, "Conditional definitions").

** size() -- write it once, right everywhere
   The size where the code is RUNNING. In the built program that is the
   target's size. Inside the compiler -- a macro body, a generator
   condition, a function the compiler evaluates to fold a call -- it is
   the compiler's own layout, which is what byte arithmetic on live
   values needs (~malloc(T.size())~, ~memcpy(dst, src, T.size())~, a
   container's element stride). Ordinary code never has to know the
   target, the pointer width or the compact layout: those belong to
   whoever builds the program.

** size_for_target() -- only for code that reasons about the target
   The size in the program being BUILT. Generated by the same generator
   under the same rule as ~size~ (skipped when the type defines it), with
   a literal til computes from the TARGET's layout. A type that defines
   its own ~size~ and no ~size_for_target~ gets one that forwards to its
   ~size~. Core writes it by hand next to ~size~ for the primitives and
   ~Bool~. It takes no target argument: the compiler knows what it is
   building for. At runtime it always equals ~size()~.

   The only code that needs it runs at compile time and decides something
   from the built program's layout: a macro, or a generator condition
   (~if T.size_for_target() <= limit~). There a plain ~size()~ answers for
   the compiler, which differs from the target only on a cross-size build
   -- a ~--usize=64~ or 32-bit target from the default compiler.

** Folding and the C compiler
   til computes both numbers; neither comes from C ~sizeof~.
   ~size_for_target()~ will fold like any pure function. A generated
   ~size()~ folds once compile-time evaluation is over, to the target's
   number, because until then the same code may still run inside the
   compiler. Only the literal is substituted; arithmetic around it is left
   to the C compiler. The C backend emits one static assert per emitted
   type that its ~sizeof~ equals til's number, so a wrong layout
   computation is a compile error, not corrupted memory.

* Derived from cmp (structs and enums)

  If a type has ~cmp := func(a: T, b: T) returns I64~, the following
  are auto-generated (each skipped if already defined):

** eq(a, b)  -> a.cmp(b).eq(0)
** neq(a, b) -> a.eq(b).not()
** lt(a, b)  -> a.cmp(b).eq(-1)
** gt(a, b)  -> a.cmp(b).eq(1)
** lte(a, b) -> a.gt(b).not()
** gte(a, b) -> a.lt(b).not()

* Derived from add+sub+unity (structs and enums)

  If a type has ~add~ and ~unity~, auto-generate (if missing):
** inc(mut self) -> self = self.add(self.unity())

  If a type has ~sub~ and ~unity~, auto-generate (if missing):
** dec(mut self) -> self = self.sub(self.unity())

  Numeric ext_structs define their own inc/dec directly (C's ++/--).

* Rangeable types (#94)

  A type is "rangeable" if it can be used with ~for i in a..b~. Nothing
  is required of it beyond METHODS, and the ones it needs all derive:

  | Method    | Used for                         | Can come from      |
  |-----------+----------------------------------+--------------------|
  | ~inc~     | ascending step                   | add + unity (auto) |
  | ~dec~     | descending step                  | sub + unity (auto) |
  | ~lt~/~gt~ | stop condition                   | cmp (auto)         |
  | ~lte~     | runtime direction check           | cmp (auto)         |

  So a struct with ~add~, ~sub~, ~unity~ and ~cmp~ is rangeable with no
  further ceremony, and all numeric builtins qualify.

** How it iterates: no Range object exists

   RANGE IS THE EXAMPLE OF ITERATING A CONTAINER-LIKE VALUE WITHOUT
   CONTAINER COST. ~a..b~ parses to ~Range.new(a, b)~, but the typer
   (~desugar_for_in_range_stmt~) never builds one: it rewrites the loop
   into a bound, a cursor and a while, calling the element's own methods
   directly.

   #+begin_src til
   for i in a..b { <body> }

   // becomes, in effect:
   {
       _re := b                       // bound, evaluated once
       mut _rc := a                   // cursor
       if _rc.lte(_re) {
           while _rc.lt(_re) { i := _rc   _rc.inc()   <body> }
       } else {
           while _rc.gt(_re) { i := _rc   _rc.dec()   <body> }
       }
   }
   #+end_src

   Consequences worth knowing:
   - ~len()~ is never computed. The old design counted steps by cloning
     the start and stepping to the end -- O(n) just to learn the length,
     before iterating.
   - The element's methods are bound STATICALLY at desugar time, so a
     builtin integer range is raw arithmetic and a user type's is a
     direct call. There is no dispatch per element.
   - When the direction is provable at compile time -- both bounds
     literal, or a literal 0 start with an unsigned element -- only ONE
     of the two loops is emitted, so the body is not built, typed or
     emitted twice.

** Rejected: Range as a real collection (recorded so it stays rejected)

   The earlier plan made ~Range~ a struct with ~len~/~get~ "the same
   interface as Vec", storing the element as ~own elem : U8~ raw bytes
   plus its type name, and stepping it through ~dyn_call(elem_type,
   "inc", ...)~ per element. It was implemented far enough to measure
   and abandoned: per-element dynamic dispatch and a per-range heap
   object made the core library's own for-in loops -- ~Str.cmp~ and
   friends -- markedly slower to compile, which is #94's recorded
   bootstrap slowdown.

   The lesson generalizes past ranges: a method-driven iteration
   protocol is right, but the methods must be resolved when the loop is
   desugared, never dispatched while it runs. Collection for-in follows
   the same rule -- it desugars to ~len()~ + ~unsafe_get(i)~, both of
   which the backend inlines, so a conforming user struct iterates at
   pointer-arithmetic cost.

** Example: user-defined rangeable type

   #+begin_src til
   Vec2 := struct {
       x : I64 = 0
       y : I64 = 0
   namespace:
       add := func(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) returns Vec2 {
           return Vec2(x = a.x.add(b.x), y = a.y.add(b.y))
       }
       sub := func(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) returns Vec2 {
           return Vec2(x = a.x.sub(b.x), y = a.y.sub(b.y))
       }
       unity := func(self: Vec2) returns Vec2 {
           return Vec2(x = self.x.sub(self.x).add(1), y = 1)
       }
       cmp := func(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) returns I64 {
           if a.x.lt(b.x) { return -1 }
           if a.x.gt(b.x) { return 1 }
           return a.y.cmp(b.y)
       }
   }
   // Auto-generated from cmp: eq, neq, lt, gt, lte, gte
   // Auto-generated from add/sub + unity: inc, dec
   // Rangeable: has inc, dec, lt, gt

   // Ascending: (0,0) -> (1,1) -> (2,2)
   for v : Vec2 in Vec2(x=0, y=0)..Vec2(x=3, y=3) { ... }
   // Descending: (3,3) -> (2,2) -> (1,1)
   for v : Vec2 in Vec2(x=3, y=3)..Vec2(x=0, y=0) { ... }
   #+end_src

   Covered by test_range_over_user_type_* in test/loops.til.

** Range element type inference

   The typer infers the element type from the ~..~ operands:
   - ~0..5~ -> both literals -> I64
   - ~0..count~ where count : U32 -> U32 (non-literal wins)
   - ~0..v.len()~ where len returns USize -> USize
   - ~for i : I32 in -5..5~ -> explicit annotation overrides

** Non-rangeable types

   A type with ~inc~/~dec~ but no ~cmp~ (and no hand-written ~lt~/~gt~)
   cannot be used with ~..~: there is no way to test the bound. The type
   can still use inc/dec directly.

   #+begin_src til
   Counter := struct {
       val : I64 = 0
   namespace:
       add := func(a: Counter, b: Counter) returns Counter {
           return Counter(val = a.val.add(b.val))
       }
       unity := func(self: Counter) returns Counter { return Counter(val = 1) }
   }
   // Gets inc auto-generated (from add + unity)
   // No cmp -> no lt/gt -> NOT rangeable
   #+end_src
